Save a mira plot as an image file

Source: R/mira_save.R
mira_save.Rd

Draws the plot in MiRA, in a browser that does not open a window, and saves it with MiRA's own export: the same picture as MiRA's camera button, with the legends and the "Visualized with MiRA" mark. Works in scripts and R Markdown, where printing a plot does nothing.

Usage

mira_save(
  plot,
  file,
  format = NULL,
  resolution = 2,
  width = 1500,
  height = 900,
  background = "grid",
  legends = TRUE,
  timeout = 60,
  mira_path = NULL
)

Arguments

plot

A mira_plot.

file

The file name, such as "fig1.png". Without an extension, format is added. Its folder must exist, and a file of that name is replaced without asking.

format

"png", "jpg" (or "jpeg") or "pdf". Without it, the extension of file decides.

resolution

A whole number from 1 to 4: 1 (screen), 2 (high, the default), 4 (print). The image is resolution times width by height pixels. A PDF page is width by height, with the picture at this resolution.

width, height

The size of MiRA's window, in pixels: whole numbers from 100 to 8000. The plot is fitted to it as in the browser. MiRA is made for windows of at least 1024 x 600: smaller ones can cut off legends and panels, and in a very small one MiRA may not draw at all (the save then times out).

background

"grid" (MiRA's grid; the map in map view), "white", or "transparent" (PNG only). The map view is saved only with "grid"; the meta-network and the dashboard not with "transparent".

legends

TRUE to include the legends (as mira_legends() sets them) and any open panels of the layer view.

timeout

Seconds to wait for MiRA to draw and save the plot. Large pictures at resolution = 4 can need more than the default.

mira_path

Character. Path to the MiRA web-app directory. If NULL (default), uses the copy bundled with the package (system.file("MiRA", package = "ggmira")).

Value

The path of the file, invisibly.

Details

Needs the chromote package and Google Chrome (or Chromium, or Microsoft Edge; chromote finds it, or set the CHROMOTE_CHROME environment variable to its path). MiRA loads its libraries and map tiles from the internet, as when a plot opens in the browser.

What is saved. Every view except the data view, which is a table (an error). The dashboard is saved as its whole page, whatever height is. A map is saved as the map with the layers' markers; the networks MiRA draws over it after a click are not part of the plot. When MiRA could not use a setting of the plot, R gives MiRA's reason as a warning and the file is still saved.

Sizes. The file holds resolution times width by height pixels, and the browser has to hold that picture in memory: a very large one (about 5000 x 4000 at resolution = 4) can fail with a browser error. Reduce resolution or the size then. Saving takes a few seconds, and longer for large pictures (timeout).

The look. Links are drawn opaque and at least one pixel of the file wide, so a dense network looks heavier at resolution = 1 than at 4, and heavier than on screen. The camera of mira_camera() is relative to the window: values copied from MiRA frame the plot the same way only when width and height match the browser window they were set in.

See also

print.mira_plot() to open the plot in the browser.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Needs the chromote package and Chrome; writes files in the working directory
library(emln)
net <- load_emln(17)
p <- mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird") +
  mira_node(color_by = "intra_degree_sum")

mira_save(p, "birds.png")
mira_save(p, "birds", format = "pdf", resolution = 4)
mira_save(p, "birds-clear.png", background = "transparent", legends = FALSE)
} # }
